\emph{Evaluate the following geometric sums or state that it diverges.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item ${\displaystyle \sum_{k=0}^{4}3^{k}}$\vfill
\item ${\displaystyle \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{-k}}$\vfill
\item ${\displaystyle \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{\pi}{4^{k}}}$\vfill
\item ${\displaystyle \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{3\cdot4}{7^{k}}^{k}}$\vfill
\item ${\displaystyle \sum_{k=2}^{\infty}3\left(-0.75\right)^{k}}$\vfill
\item ${\displaystyle \sum_{k=1}^{\infty}e^{-2k}}$\vfill
\item ${\displaystyle \sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{3^{k-1}}{4^{k+1}}}$\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\emph{For the following telescoping series, find a formula for the
$n^{\mbox{th}}$ term of the sequence of partial sums $\{S_{n}\}$.
Then evaluate the ${\displaystyle \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}S_{n}}$
to obtain the value of the series or state that it diverges.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item ${\displaystyle \sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\left(\frac{1}{k+1}-\frac{1}{k+2}\right)}$\vfill
\item ${\displaystyle \sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\left(\frac{1}{k+2}-\frac{1}{k+3}\right)}$\vfill
\end{enumerate}
